qa_pair.question: A Bournemouth trade scheme: six trade counter units of 2,600 ft² NIA at £225/ft², plus one 3,200 ft² mezzanine office at £240/ft². 90% efficiency, a single build trade at £105/ft², professional fees 11%, contingency 5%. Other costs are £150,000 of planning and S106 plus the CIL on the gross internal area at £40 per square metre. Senior debt 60% of construction at 7.5% over an 18-month build and 3 months of sales, 1.5% arrangement fee, S-curve spend. Solve the land value at a 20% target profit on GDV, with 6.8% acquisition costs and disposal at 1.5% agency and 0.5% legal. What is the gross development value, in pounds?

For that same Bournemouth scheme — six 2,600 ft² trade counter units at £225/ft², one 3,200 ft² mezzanine at £240/ft², 90% efficiency, £105/ft² build, 11% fees, 5% contingency, £150,000 planning and S106 plus CIL at £40/m², 60% LTC at 7.5% over 18 months plus 3 months of sales with a 1.5% arrangement fee and S-curve spend, 20% target profit on GDV, 6.8% acquisition, 1.5% agency and 0.5% legal — what residual land value does it support, to the nearest pound?
On that same Bournemouth appraisal, what is the profit on cost as a percentage, to one decimal place?
What is the Stamp Duty Land Tax on a £1,850,000 non-residential purchase in England, in pounds?
What is the Stamp Duty Land Tax on a £950,000 residential purchase in England where the higher rate for an additional dwelling applies, in pounds?
A scheme has 20,888.89 ft² of gross internal area and the charging schedule sets CIL at £40 per square metre. What is the levy, to the nearest pound?

A build-to-rent block of 48 apartments, each 620 ft², letting at £32/ft²/year with a 4% void allowance. Non-recoverable outgoings are 5% of rent, the all-risks yield is 4.25% and purchaser's costs are 6.8%. What is the capital value net of purchaser's costs, to the nearest pound?

Two options on the same 24,000 ft² site. Option A sells at a blended £245/ft² and builds at £118/ft². Option B sells at £265/ft² and builds at £132/ft². Both target 20% profit on GDV. Which option supports the higher residual land value — answer A or B?

Thirty flats of 850 ft² at £450/ft², 88% efficiency, an all-in build rate of £165/ft², 11% fees, 5% contingency, CIL at £60 per square metre, £240,000 of S106, 1.5% agency and 0.5% legal, 60% LTC at 8% over a 20-month build and 4 months of sales with a 1.5% arrangement fee, 20% target profit and 6.8% acquisition costs, with no asking price quoted. What residual land value does the scheme support, to the nearest pound?
